Note::html_unescape¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::html_unescape() const

Resolve HTML Entity References Back To Characters¶

html_unescape() is the inverse of html_escape: it scans each cell for &…; entity references and replaces the ones it recognizes with the characters they denote. Use it to recover plain text from a value that was previously escaped, or that arrived from an HTML source.

What is recognized¶

  • The named references &amp; &lt; &gt; &quot; &apos; — and &#39;, which html_escape emits for '.

  • Numeric character references: decimal &#N; and hexadecimal &#xH; (case-insensitive x), for any code point up to U+10FFFF. The code point is encoded as UTF-8 in the result, so &#8364; and &#x20AC; both become € and &#x1F600; becomes 😀.

This is a deliberately small set — the five markup characters plus numeric escapes — not the full HTML5 named-character-reference table. An entity the method does not know (&copy;, &nbsp;, a misspelling) is left exactly as written, and a bare & with no ; is also left untouched. Nothing is dropped, so unknown markup passes through rather than disappearing.

The operation works on UTF-8 text and bytes-mode Notes, preserves shape, keeps the encoding tag, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: Named References¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a &amp; b &lt;c&gt; &quot;q&quot; &#39;x&apos;"})
                 .html_unescape()
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["a & b <c> \"q\" 'x'"]

(The \" in the printed form is the Note printer escaping the double quote; the cell contains a literal ".)

Example 2: Numeric References, Decimal And Hex¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"&#65;&#x41; &#8364; &#x1F600;"}).html_unescape() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["AA € 😀"]

&#65; and &#x41; both resolve to A.

Example 3: Unknown Entities Survive Verbatim¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"&foo; &amp &notreal;"}).html_unescape() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["&foo; &amp &notreal;"]

&foo; and &notreal; are not recognized; &amp has no semicolon. All three are left as-is.

Example 4: Round Trip With html_escape¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a & b < c > d \" e ' f"})
                 .html_escape()
                 .html_unescape()
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["a & b < c > d \" e ' f"]
